title: A block dropped into a cup is the one-year container skill
summary: By about a first birthday, most babies put something in a container, such as a block in a cup, the U.S. CDC says.
body: The CDC page for age one lists putting something in a container, like a block in a cup, as a cognitive item. Its bar for most is 75 percent of children or higher by that birthday. The page says the Learn the Signs handouts do not replace a standardized, validated developmental screen. This is one country's checklist. It does not declare a particular infant late, and it is not worded as something every baby must pass. Hunting for a toy hidden under a blanket is another line and is left off this card.
